title: Maximal Coverage Location-Allocation Using Geospatial Data
text: Assessing planning infrastructure service networks, given dispersed demand, limited capacity, accessibility targets, concerns spatial justice, central policy challenge. Problems type commonly referred Maximal Coverage Location-Allocation (MCLA) spatial optimization problems. locationallocation R package provides tools solving MCLA problems geospatial data. builds widely used spatial libraries R, follows tidyverse principles, integrates seamlessly broader tidyverse ecosystem. package can generate travel-time maps optimize placement facilities infrastructure according accessibility criteria, can weighted one variables user-defined function. Potential applications package extend domains public infrastructure assessment planning (public services provision, e.g. transport, social services, healthcare, parks), urban environmental climate risk reduction interventions, logistics hubs allocation, commercial strategic decisions.

The achieved coverage share is 99.06013%. allocation_data |>   allocation_plot(naples_shape, facilities = naples_fountains) library(sf)  allocation_data <-   naples_population |>   allocation_discrete(     bb_area = naples_shape,     candidate = naples_shape |> st_sample(20),     facilities = naples_fountains,     n_fac = 5,     traveltime = traveltime_data,     weights = NULL,     objectiveminutes = 15,     objectiveshare = NULL,     approach = "norm",     exp_demand = 1,     exp_weights = 1,     par = FALSE   ) #> ℹ 5 facilities allocated within the 15 minutes threshold. title: Maximal coverage location-allocation — allocation
text: demand RasterLayer single-layer SpatRaster object demand (e.g., number people per cell), geographic coordinates (WGS 84). defines grid analysis. bb_area sf object polygon(s) area interest. facilities sf object existing facilities, NULL existing facilities. Required allocation() (use facilities = NULL explicitly allocate scratch); optional allocation_discrete() (default: NULL). traveltime (optional) output traveltime() function, whose friction surface reused avoid downloading downscaling . travel times facilities recomputed surface. NULL, friction surface computed friction() using mode res_output (default: NULL). mode (optional) character string indicating mode transport. Options "fastest" "walk" (default: "walk"). title: locationallocation 0.2.0
text: allocation_discrete() now uses deterministic greedy algorithm described package paper, refined vertex substitution (Teitz & Bart, 1968), instead random sampling. travel time candidate computed , solver much faster returns optimal near-optimal solutions. n_samples deprecated ignored; par now parallelizes travel time computations. allocation() now implements greedy step package paper (lazy greedy heuristic): iteration, heuristic score shortlists promising locations, actual catchments computed, new facility goes evaluated location covers uncovered demand. Previously, facility placed directly highest-scoring cell. greedy solution refined vertex substitution (Teitz & Bart, 1968) pattern search new locations around facility, , objectiveshare, dropping facilities long target still met. New arguments: shortlist (locations evaluated per iteration) refine (set FALSE faster, greedy-solutions). default heur now "kd". Naples example (downscaled friction surface previous version), 99% coverage reached 25 new facilities instead 37, matching near-optimal reference solution computed dense grid candidate locations. Travel times allocation() allocation_discrete() computed routing graph built per problem, instead rebuilding gdistance::accCost() call. Results identical, computation 8 times faster Naples example. Travel times aligned demand grid double precision (terra::resample() rounds values single precision). resolutions finer 1 km (res_output < 1000), friction() now follows rules used build MAP surfaces, fastest mode transport within cell takes precedence. "walk" mode, MAP assigns 5 km/h roads urban land, walking surface resampled finer grid without changing values (OpenStreetMap download needed). "fastest" mode, cells crossed OpenStreetMap road get speed fastest road class crossing (new road_speeds argument; defaults default_road_speeds(), free-flow speeds OSRM car profile), cells MAP walking surface. New roads argument supply road network instead downloading ; cache = TRUE, downloaded road network cached disk, failed downloads retried. dowscaling_model_type deprecated ignored, dissever dependency removed. allocation() gains n_fac, maximum number new facilities. finite n_fac, objectiveshare can NULL allocate exactly n_fac facilities. allocation() accepts facilities = NULL allocate facilities scratch. allocation() allocation_discrete(), traveltime used friction surface: travel times facilities recomputed unmasked surface, exactly new facilities. Previously, demand cells near boundary bb_area counted uncovered even next existing facility. traveltime NULL, friction() run. traveltime() uses facilities within bounding box bb_area sources (previously inside polygon), since facilities just outside boundary still serve demand inside . Travel times aligned demand grid nearest-neighbor resampling, coverage reported allocation functions exactly matches travel_time map. Coverage checks objectiveshare now use weighted demand. allocation_plot() gains facilities argument plot existing facilities, plot functions draw boundary bb_area show unreachable cells gray. Inputs CRS accepted sf objects (transformed WGS 84), demand/weights can SpatRaster objects. weights different grid resampled grid demand.
